submission.justification: Crystal-K3 has the best resolution (~2.98% FWHM at 5 cm), but its intrinsic background of 2.0 ± 0.2 counts/kg/day (Q1 2026 assay, caused by contamination inside the crystal itself) is 4x the facility budget of 0.5 counts/kg/day. Shielding cannot remove background from inside the crystal, so K3 fails the low-background constraint. K2 (0.30 counts/kg/day) and K1 (0.10) both meet the budget. K2 resolves much better (~4.4-4.7% vs ~8.7% for K1 at 5 cm), so K2 gives the best resolution among the options that meet the constraint. Scanning K2 thickness gave: 2 cm 5.12%, 3 cm 4.87%, 4 cm 4.49%, 4.5 cm 4.47/4.48%, 5 cm 4.72/4.67%, 5.5 cm 4.36/4.34%, 6 cm 4.54%, 8 cm 5.24%, 10 cm 6.34%. The best repeated value is at 5.5 cm (~4.35%). Repeat runs agree to within about 0.05% at a given thickness. The non-monotonic 5 cm point suggests some structure in the model, so the 4.5-5.5 cm region should be checked when the prototype is commissioned. Caveat: the 0.5 counts/kg/day budget applies per kilogram. A 5.5 cm crystal has more mass, so its total count rate rises, but the per-kg figure stays within budget.

requirements.requirement: Goal: best possible energy resolution at 662 keV
requirements.evidence: K2 at 5.5 cm gives ~4.35% FWHM (two runs: 4.356, 4.335), the best of all K2 thicknesses scanned from 2 to 10 cm. K3 (~2.98%) is better but is excluded by the background constraint. K1 is ~8.7%.
